name: First Switched Local Hole
definition: On projected coordinates $p,q$, partition the punctured square $P_{\{p,q\}}$ as $D=\{\varnothing\}$, $Z_0=\{\{p\}\}$, and $Z_1=\{\{q\}\}$. Form $L=((D\cup Z_0)\times\{0\})\cup((D\cup Z_1)\times\{1\})$.
properties: The resulting family is a four-vertex path. Its contraction is the punctured square, but neither section contains that punctured square: its arms lie on opposite sides and meet at the duplicated central vertex. The missing square is therefore a canonical contraction hole that is not transported from one source-side hole.
